notes: Read SKILL.md and references/data-access.md, references/provenance.md, references/publishing.md in full. Guides the agent through DataLad/git-annex: cloning and fetching datasets (OpenNeuro, DANDI, datasets.datalad.org), recording provenance with datalad run/rerun/containers-run, saving, dropping content, and publishing to Git plus storage siblings.

Medium: the agent is told to install packages (`uv pip install git-annex`, pinned `datalad==1.6.5`, `datalad-container==1.2.6` at SKILL.md:55-60), run shell commands that download data, create GitHub repositories and S3 special remotes and `datalad push` (SKILL.md:231-235, publishing.md:136-140) using the user's GitHub token and AWS/DataLad credentials, and drop local annex content. Acceptable because the installs are pinned official PyPI packages, publication examples are labelled illustrative and require the user's own credentials, `datalad drop` is shown with its default availability safety check and the reckless overrides are explained as data-losing (data-access.md:127-133), and the skill tells the agent never to commit credentials (publishing.md:205-206).

Publishing creates remote resources and can expose data; users should confirm sibling targets and bucket access policy before a push. Mentions that git-annex is AGPL-licensed software (SKILL.md:74-75) and an acknowledgment of an MIT-licensed community plugin that informed topic scope (SKILL.md:324-329); neither is bundled. The optional `bids` related skill (SKILL.md:298) is not required. publishing.md:127-129 only documents what `push -f gitpush` does; no forced push is instructed.
